item.title: Caveling
item.description: The Caveling is the basic hostile mob of The Undergrounds, found near the starting area. Low health and telegraphed attacks make it an easy first combat target. Tips Attacks are telegraphed — dodge sideways, not backwards Drops Caveling Remains used in early crafting

item.title: Caveling Brute
item.description: The Caveling Brute is a slow but hard-hitting melee enemy found in The Undergrounds and The Clay Caves. It hits much harder than a normal Caveling — don’t tank its swings. Combat tips Dodge, don’t block: its swings are telegraphed; sidestep rather than trading hits Kite it: it’s slower than the player, so attack between its swing cooldowns Iron gear comfort: with 140 HP and 16 damage, it’s manageable in copper but much safer in tin+ Drops Caveling Remains (common) — salvage/repair material Iron Ore (common) — early source before you reach The Forgotten Ruins

item.title: Core Keeper Achievements
item.description: Achievements in Core Keeper are the Steam trophy trackers that shadow your run: roughly sixty trophies split between boss kills, skill masteries, rare collectibles and a handful of deliberately silly hidden tasks. Many show their condition up front, while the hidden ones stay blank until you stumble into them. How the list is structured Visible trophies hand you the objective in the Steam client; hidden trophies show only a name and an icon, so spoilers are built into the design.

item.title: Core Keeper Base Building Guide — Room Rules, NPC Housing and Automation
item.description: A good Core Keeper base is more than a pile of chests. This base building guide covers the room system, NPC move-in rules, bed mechanics and the automation basics that keep your underground hub running while you explore. Room rules that actually matter Rooms are the core building block of a Core Keeper base. The game recognizes a room when: The enclosed area is between 2×2 and 8×8 tiles (smaller or larger rooms don’t register) It has a door and a bed It contains the required item for the NPC you want (each NPC has a specific item) No players are within 30 tiles of the room for roughly a minute If any condition fails, the room won’t count — and NPCs won’t move in.

item.title: Core Keeper Boss Guide — All 7 Bosses, Drops, Locations and Strategies
item.description: Core Keeper’s boss order follows your tool progression: three bosses around the Core must fall before it powers up, then the outer-ring titans open endgame content. This Core Keeper boss guide lists every boss, where they spawn, how to summon them and what they drop. The three early bosses (power up the Core) Defeat all three and place their drops on the effigies next to the Core to activate it.

item.title: Core Keeper Cooking
item.description: Cooking is how you turn raw foraged ingredients into dishes that punch far above their weight. Dropping two ingredients into a Cooking Pot produces a meal with stronger buffs, longer duration, and hidden stat combinations you’d never see from eating them raw. Understanding the hidden math behind the pot is what separates a good survivor from an endgame-ready one. How the Cooking Pot works Set a Cooking Pot down on any flat surface, walk up to it, and interact to open its interface.

item.title: Core Keeper Cooking & Food Buff Guide — Best Recipes and How Buffs Stack
item.description: Food in Core Keeper isn’t just hunger — the right dishes are pre-boss loadouts. This cooking guide explains how food buffs work, which ingredients give the strongest effects, and the best combos before each fight. How food buffs work Food value refills your hunger; hunger loss only reduces max health and stats — you can’t die of starvation. Cooked ingredients give Regen, max health, armor, damage and speed buffs with a duration.

item.title: Core Keeper First Hour Guide — World Creation, Tools and Your First Boss
item.description: The Core Keeper getting started experience is built around one loop: craft a workbench, make stronger tools, mine tougher walls, find better ores, and repeat. This guide walks through world creation, the first hour, and the three early bosses you need to beat before the Core powers up. World creation: what to pick Select Start Game from the main menu to create a world. You can also join a friend’s world from the Steam friends list — Core Keeper has native multiplayer with no dedicated server required, and more than the officially stated 8 players can connect.

item.title: Core Keeper Fishing
item.description: Fishing is a leisure skill in Core Keeper that quietly pays for itself: toss a rod into any water tile, wait for a bite, and pull up fish, ore, kelp, loose tools or even locked chests. It also feeds the cooking loop, because a well-cooked fish dish hands you a real damage buff right before a boss attempt. How a catch actually works Stand next to any water source and cast the bobber.

item.title: Core Keeper Gardening
item.description: Gardening lets you turn loose seeds into a repeatable supply of food, fiber and crafting materials. You till a patch of suitable dirt, plant a seed, keep it watered, and pick the mature crop by hand. Nearly every harvest also feeds the cooking loop, so a well-kept farm is the backbone of long-term survivability in the underground caves. How the farming loop works A typical farm follows the same short cycle every run:

item.title: Core Keeper Mechanics
item.description: Mechanics is the set of hidden formulas behind every number in Core Keeper: how your attacks scale, how much punishment your armour actually soaks, how power-ups wear off, and why bosses suddenly feel twice as scary with a friend online. Most players beat the early game by feel, but once you start min-maxing around Scarlet, Octarine and legendary gear, the order these bonuses apply decides whether a build is strong or merely okay.

item.title: Core Keeper Mining
item.description: Mining means breaking walls to dig out metal ore and other materials as you explore. Early on you chew through dirt, stone and ore veins by hand, but the real bottleneck is damage thresholds: every wall type absorbs a flat chunk of your mining power before your pickaxe starts actually chipping it. Once Drills unlock later, giant Ore Boulders become a far more efficient supply of metal — but until then, knowing which pickaxe to craft next is the single biggest speed-up available.

item.title: Core Keeper Mods Guide — Where to Download, How to Install and Essential Mods
item.description: Core Keeper supports official modding through Steam Workshop and mod.io, with community content managed by the CoreLib framework. This modding guide covers where to find mods, how to install them, and the most useful quality-of-life mods. Where to get mods Platform What it is Notes Steam Workshop Official in-game mod browser One-click subscribe & install; requires the game mod.io Cross-platform mod repository Browsable online, official Core Keeper page CoreLib Community mod framework / loader Most mods depend on it; install first Check the Mods hub for an indexed list of popular mods and their patch compatibility.

item.title: Core Keeper Ore Tier Guide — Pickaxe Progression and Where Each Ore Spawns
item.description: Core Keeper’s world is generated in rings around the Core, and each ring holds different ores. This Core Keeper ore guide maps every ore to the pickaxe tier and biome you need — so you never waste time mining with the wrong tool. Pickaxe tiers at a glance Pickaxe Workbench Materials Mines Wood Pickaxe Starting inventory Wood Soft dirt walls only Copper Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Copper Bar, 10 Wood Copper, Tin Tin Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Tin Bar, 10 Wood Iron Iron Pickaxe Iron Anvil 8 Iron Bar, 10 Wood Gold, Scarlet Gold Pickaxe Gold Anvil 8 Gold Bar, 10 Wood Harder ores, faster Scarlet Pickaxe Scarlet Workbench 8 Scarlet Bar, 10 Wood Best pre-endgame speed You can technically mine anywhere from the start — but stronger walls block exploration until your pickaxe tier catches up.

item.title: Core Keeper Scenes
item.description: Scenes are the hand-designed set pieces scattered across an otherwise procedural world. The tunnels, ores and dirt around you are generated algorithmically, but a shrine, a buried chest room, a merchant’s cell or a maze is a pre-built structure stamped into the map whole. Learning to recognize them by shape turns routine digging into targeted treasure hunting. What makes a scene different from terrain Most of the world is rolled on the fly, but scenes follow their own rules:

item.title: Core Keeper Seasonal Events
item.description: Seasonal events are short, theme-driven celebrations that transform the underworld for a few weeks every year — pumpkins in autumn, snow and presents in winter, cherry blossoms in spring. During each window, certain enemies and bosses get a visual reskin, the main-menu logo changes to match the theme, and a roster of exclusive food, vanity and building items becomes available. Most of that limited loot is sold by the travelling Seasonal Merchant, so collecting the full set depends on logging in at the right time.

item.title: Core Keeper Skills
item.description: Skills are your character’s passive progression track. Rather than spending points by hand, you earn experience simply by doing the activities the game already expects — swinging a pickaxe, swinging a sword, running around, planting seeds — and that experience slowly fills each skill bar toward level 100. Every discipline grants a small permanent bonus as it levels, and every fifth level hands you a talent point to spend in that skill’s own tree.

item.title: Core Keeper World
item.description: World generation in Core Keeper is radial and deterministic. Every map is an underground layer that starts at The Core in the middle and spreads outward in rings; beyond a certain distance the plane is effectively endless. A hidden seed value baked into your save decides how those rings rotate, where each boss sits, and the exact shape of every chasm. Once you understand the ring layout, “where do I go next?

item.title: Core Keeper World Seeds Guide — How Seeds Shape Your World
item.description: Every Core Keeper world is generated from a seed — the number you pick at world creation. The seed decides where each biome ring sits, which direction you find the Clay Caves, and roughly where the early bosses spawn. This guide explains how seed generation works and how to use seeds with friends. What a seed controls Aspect Seed-dependent Biome angles Yes — Clay Caves / Forgotten Ruins each occupy half of the world beyond the chasm; the exact angle varies by seed Outer biome order Yes — the three outer biomes (Azeos’ Wilderness, Sunken Sea, Mold) rotate counter-clockwise per seed Boss placement Partly — Glurch spawns ~65 tiles in a random angle; boss arc segments shift with the seed World shape / ring distances No — the ring band structure (0–140, 150–450, 450–520, 520–1200+) is the same for every world In short: the seed is a rotation and placement key, not a terrain generator.

item.title: Core Keeper 新手入門指南（繁體中文）
item.description: 本篇以繁體中文整理《Core Keeper》開局 1-2 小時的關鍵流程，配合本站工具可快速上手。 開局流程（前 60 分鐘） 採集：在核心（The Core）四周採集銅礦與錫礦，敲碎木材與纖維。 工具：製作工作台 → 銅鎬（採礦速度 +26-30，耐久 400）；錫鎬可採集鐵礦（+42 採礦傷害）。 光源與背包：製作火把與箱子，隨身帶 1-2 個床（避免死亡後跑圖）。 探索方向：優先沿核心向外探索，找出三個早期 Boss 的方位（Glurch / Ghorm / Hive Mother）。 鎬子升級路線 鎬 等級 採礦傷害 耐久 解鎖內容 銅鎬 1 +26-30 400 基礎礦物 錫鎬 3 +42 400 鐵礦、黏土洞穴 鐵鎬 5 +58 400 金礦、熔爐 金鎬 7 +74 400 猩紅礦、外環 猩紅鎬 9 +90 400 隕石、Boss 戰 數據來源：本站 Mining Matrix 工具（對應遊戲版本 Verified against game version 1.3.0.6 — source: corekeeper.atma.gg. ）。

item.title: Furnace
item.description: The Furnace is the first ore-processing station in Core Keeper, smelting raw ore into bars for tools and equipment. It’s the bridge between mining copper/tin and crafting metal gear. What it processes Copper Ore → Copper Bar Tin Ore → Tin Bar Later: Iron, Gold and Scarlet bars for higher tiers The parallel furnace trick You can’t speed up a single furnace’s smelting time — but you can build several furnaces and process ores concurrently.

item.title: Iron Pickaxe
item.description: The Iron Pickaxe is the tier-3 mining tool in Core Keeper, crafted at the Iron Workbench after you reach The Forgotten Ruins. It unlocks gold and scarlet ore mining, the gateway to late-early-game equipment. Use Mines Gold Ore and Scarlet Ore Faster on earlier ores than the Tin Pickaxe Required before the first three bosses for the recommended Iron gear tier Crafting path Copper Pickaxe → mine Tin in The Clay Caves Tin Pickaxe → mine Iron in The Forgotten Ruins Iron Pickaxe → mine Gold / Scarlet for Iron-tier equipment

item.title: Item Crafting Calculator
item.description: The Core Keeper item crafting calculator expands any recipe into its full crafting tree. item.title: Seed Finder
item.description: The Core Keeper seed finder helps you pick a good world seed before you start. Every world is generated from a numeric seed — it determines biome rotation, boss spawn arcs and fixed scenes, while terrain details are generated chunk-by-chunk as you explore. How to use Enter a numeric seed and hit Preview Layout to see the deterministic ring structure: the Core in the center, the inner ring (Clay Caves + Forgotten Ruins, 150–450 tiles), the Great Wall (450–520) and the three outer biomes (520–1200).

item.title: The Clay Caves
item.description: The Clay Caves is one of the two inner-ring biomes (150–450 tiles from the Core), home to the game’s tin ore and the Larva Hive dungeon where the Hive Mother waits. Location Cross the chasm around The Undergrounds with a Wood Bridge. The Clay Caves and The Forgotten Ruins each occupy one half of the world beyond the chasm — the exact angle varies by seed, so if you find the Ruins first, walk the opposite direction from the Core.

item.title: The Undergrounds
item.description: The Undergrounds (the Dirt Biome) is the safe starting ring around The Core, spanning 0–140 tiles. It is also the default biome filling the gaps between other biomes. What you find Copper and tin ore for the first tools Wood, stone and early food crops The first three bosses’ summon points at fixed arcs Tips Build your first base within 140 tiles of the Core for safety Follow Ghorm’s track to explore outward efficiently
